% overpic pictures, and LaTeX pictures that hold an \includegraphics, over
% PDF, PNG, and JPEG pictures with no .xbb file beside them. Each one
% builds at its size in the PDF, which the edges drawn along its bottom and
% left side, or a frame, show in its image. Cases: a share of the text
% width, no size, trim and clip, scale with a grid and tics, abs and unit
% with a height through \graphicspath, permil, \setOverpic, the Overpic
% environment, a LaTeX picture, a figure with angle and a caption, no
% extension, italic and math labels, a minipage, a table cell, a JPEG, a
% PDF with its MediaBox away from 0 0, a PDF with a CropBox, the second
% page of a PDF, a PNG at 144 dpi, a folder in the name, a LaTeX picture
% at natural size, and a subfigure. The last overpic has its .xbb file,
% which the fix must not break. Nor must it change a plain \includegraphics
% of a PNG without its .xbb file, outside any picture, sized with width,
% scale, or height after an overpic of the same PNG.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\usepackage{overpic}
\usepackage{subcaption}
% the bottom and left edges of an overpic, at its size
\newcommand\edges{\put(0,0){\rule{\width}{0.4pt}}\put(0,0){\rule{0.4pt}{\height}}}
\setlength{\fboxsep}{0pt}
\begin{document}
\section{Overpic}
\begin{overpic}[width=0.5\textwidth]{test-overpic-box.pdf}
\edges
\put(10,10){A}
\end{overpic}
After share.

\begin{overpic}{test-overpic-box.pdf}
\edges
\put(10,10){B}
\end{overpic}

\put(10,10){C}

\end{overpic}
